Subject: COI and endorsement for Redwood order form

Hi Tessa,

Attached is our insurer's certificate for the upcoming order form (see VectorGrid_Certificate.pdf). Per our broker, the carrier is unwilling to add 'Redwood Inference, Inc.' as Additional Insured on the primary policy, but they can issue a supplemental endorsement with near-equivalent wording. I attached the draft endorsement the carrier proposed (VectorGrid_Endorsement_proposal.pdf).

We want to keep the deal moving — what exact language would satisfy Redwood? If legal needs to review the attached endorsement, loop them in and let us know whether the proposal is acceptable or if we need to get an endorsement from a different carrier (which will take longer).

Thanks,
Jordan Lee
Head of Contracts
VectorGrid

Attachments: VectorGrid_Certificate.pdf, VectorGrid_Endorsement_proposal.pdf

From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: COI and endorsement for Redwood order form

Jordan — thanks for the quick turn. I downloaded both attachments and did a quick pass. Two asks from our side so we can close procurement: 

1) Naming: we need the endorsement to expressly name 'Redwood Inference, Inc., its affiliates and their officers, directors, and employees' as Additional Insured (or equivalent phrase).
2) Primary / Noncontrib + Waiver: endorsement or certificate needs language that makes VectorGrid's policy primary and non-contributory with a waiver of subrogation in favor of Redwood.

Aditya — looping you and Kim for legal / broker confirmation. If the carrier's wording is materially different, what is the threshold where we escalate to an insurance exception? Can we accept the current endorsement proposal if the carrier adds a defined limits clause?

Jordan — asap we need an updated PDF with the exact naming or a one-paragraph carrier confirmation by email that meets both asks above. If it helps, I've attached our internal COI checklist (Redwood_COI_requirements_v2.pdf) with the line items they typically match.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_COI_requirements_v2.pdf

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@vectorgrid.io>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: COI and endorsement for Redwood order form

Tessa / Jordan — quick legal take after reviewing the draft endorsement:

- Naming: the exact phrase matters. We prefer: 'Redwood Inference, Inc., its subsidiaries and affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, and employees' as Additional Insured. If carrier refuses that exact string, we can accept 'Redwood Inference, Inc. and its affiliates' only if the endorsement also lists the policyholder name (VectorGrid) and the order form/contract reference (Order Form #4387).
- Primary/non-contributory: must be explicit. A statement that the carrier's coverage will be 'primary and non-contributory' is required.
- Waiver of subrogation: explicit waiver in favor of Redwood on the applicable lines (GL, Auto, if applicable).
- Retro date / prior acts: For professional services exposures, we usually want a retroactive date no later than the start of the engagement (2025-08-01). If the policy is claims-made, carrier must confirm retro date or provide occurrence form.

If VectorGrid's carrier can't provide the naming, then procurement should route an insurance exception (approval) — but that requires a compensating control (SLA holdback or higher limits). Kim, can you advise on broker-level tradeoffs?

Jordan — if you can ask the carrier for a one-paragraph email that states the endorsement language and confirms primary/non-contributory and waiver, legal can provisionally accept while we route any exception. Otherwise we will need the insurer to reissue the endorsement with the exact line items.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@vectorgrid.io>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Meera Patel <meera.patel@vectorgrid.io>
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: COI and endorsement for Redwood order form

Aditya / Tessa — appreciate the clarity. I heard back from our broker this morning. Carrier will not use the full 'subsidiaries and affiliates' string, but they can issue an endorsement naming: 'Redwood Inference, Inc. and its affiliates' and explicitly reference Order Form #4387. They also confirmed via broker note that the endorsement includes primary/non-contributory language and a waiver of subrogation for General Liability. See attached draft endorsement (VectorGrid_Endorsement_proposal.pdf) — highlighted section is their proposed naming and liability language.

Broker note (verbatim): "Carrier confirms endorsement will reference Contract ID and provide primary/non-contributory wording; waiver applies to GL only; retro date is 2025-06-01. Auto coverage endorsement not available on this policy."

If Redwood can accept GL-only waiver and the narrower naming, we can move to execution immediately; otherwise we will need to escalate.

Jordan

Attachments: VectorGrid_Endorsement_proposal.pdf

From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@vectorgrid.io>

Subject: Re: COI and endorsement for Redwood order form

Thanks everyone — plan and next steps: 

1) Aditya: legal is okay to accept the carrier's narrower naming ('Redwood Inference, Inc. and its affiliates') provided the endorsement explicitly references Order Form #4387 and confirms primary/non-contributory for GL plus waiver of subrogation for GL. We will escalate only if the broker's written confirmation contradicts the draft endorsement.
2) Kim: please confirm whether GL-only waiver + no auto endorsement is acceptable from a broker/underwriting perspective or whether procurement should request increased limits elsewhere.
3) Jordan: please ask the broker to (a) attach a one-paragraph carrier confirmation email and (b) reissue a PDF endorsement with the Order Form reference in text. Once we have those two things we can close insurance evidence and proceed to DocuSign.

I'll update the HubSpot deal and mark insurance evidence pending until attachments arrive.
